subject.title: [Feature]: Add JSON-RPC bindings for language-agnostic plugins

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class JSON-RPC child-process plugin ABI through the linked manifest/SDK direction, narrow it to fewer plugin surfaces, or defer it?
rationale: This is a new public plugin SDK and process-execution boundary, so automation cannot decide the permanent ABI, supported registration set, or security/lifecycle contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Review the linked PR as the canonical path
options.body: Continue with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98005 and settle the ABI, supported surfaces, and proof requirements there before closing this issue.

options.title: Narrow the first version
options.body: Accept the direction but limit v1 to a smaller surface such as tools and async hooks while leaving HTTP routes or Gateway methods for follow-up design.

options.title: Defer the ABI
options.body: Keep current in-process TypeScript plugin registration and ask non-TypeScript plugins to use one-off adapters until the plugin API direction is clearer.

recommendation.title: Review the linked PR as the canonical path
recommendation.body: Continue with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98005 and settle the ABI, supported surfaces, and proof requirements there before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest current history across plugin SDK, manifest, and docs surfaces that would own the public contract shape.
